name: Scientific Paper
description: Research paper structure: idea, context and motivation, related work, method, experimental design, results, discussion.

sections.title: Title and Abstract
sections.objective: Summarise the whole paper so that a reader can decide in one minute whether to read it.

content.markdown:
_A specific, informative title (ideally stating the contribution or main finding)._

[Working title]

subs.title: Abstract
subs.objective: Write it last, but keep a draft from day one to stay focused.

content.markdown:
_150–250 words, one or two sentences per point:_

1. **Context:** [the broader area and why it matters]
2. **Gap:** [what is missing or unsolved]
3. **Approach:** [what we propose]
4. **Results:** [main quantitative findings]
5. **Implications:** [why the results matter]

sections.title: Introduction
sections.objective: Motivate the problem, state the research questions and the contributions clearly.

children.title: Context and Motivation
children.objective: Explain the broader context and why the problem is important now.

content.markdown: _From general to specific: the field, the practical or scientific need, evidence that the problem matters (numbers, trends, citations)._

children.title: Problem Statement and Research Questions
children.objective: Formulate the precise problem and the questions the paper answers.

subs.title: Research questions
subs.objective: Every RQ must be answered explicitly in the Results or Discussion.

content.markdown:
- **RQ1:** [Question answerable by the experiments]
- **RQ2:** [Question]
- **RQ3:** [Question]

children.title: Contributions
children.objective: List what is new in this work, in verifiable terms.

content.markdown:
This paper makes the following contributions:

1. [A new method / model / dataset / analysis …]
2. [An evaluation showing …]
3. [An open-source implementation / artifact …]

children.title: Paper Organisation
children.objective: Guide the reader through the rest of the paper.

content.markdown: Section 2 reviews related work. Section 3 presents [...]. Section 4 describes the experimental design, Section 5 reports the results, Section 6 discusses them and Section 7 concludes.

sections.title: Background and Related Work
sections.objective: Give the background needed and position the work against the state of the art.

children.title: Background
children.objective: Introduce the concepts and notation the reader needs.

content.markdown: _Define the concepts, models and notation used in the rest of the paper._

children.title: Related Work
children.objective: Group prior work by approach and explain the limitations this paper addresses.

subs.title: Comparison with prior work
subs.objective: Keep the BibTeX file in References and cite by key.

content.markdown:
| Work | Approach | Strengths | Limitations | How we differ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Author et al., Year] | [Method] | [...] | [...] | [...] |

children.title: Research Gap
children.objective: State precisely what is missing in the state of the art.

content.markdown: _One paragraph: despite [prior work], no approach [does X] under [conditions Y]._

sections.title: Proposed Approach
sections.objective: Describe the method so that it could be reimplemented from the paper alone.

children.title: Overview
children.objective: Give the big picture of the approach before the details.

content.code:
flowchart LR
  data[(Input data)] --> pre[Preprocessing]
  pre --> model[Proposed model]
  model --> post[Post-processing]
  post --> out[/Output/]

children.title: Formalisation
children.objective: Define the problem and the method formally.

content.markdown: _Given [inputs], find [outputs] that minimise/maximise [objective], subject to [constraints]._

subs.title: Objective function
subs.objective: Replace with the actual formulation and define every symbol.

children.title: Algorithm
children.objective: Present the algorithm and its complexity.

content.markdown: _Time and space complexity, with respect to [n, d, …]._

sections.title: Experimental Design
sections.objective: Plan experiments that answer each research question convincingly and reproducibly.

children.title: Hypotheses
children.objective: State the testable hypotheses linked to the research questions.

content.markdown:
| Hypothesis | Related RQ | Experiment | Supported if |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H1: [statement] | RQ1 | [Exp. 1] | [e.g. significant improvement, p < 0.05] |

children.title: Datasets and Setup
children.objective: Describe data, splits and the experimental environment.

content.markdown:
| Dataset | Size | Task | Split | Source / license |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Name] | [N samples] | [Classification] | [70/15/15] | [URL, CC-BY] |

children.title: Baselines
children.objective: Choose the methods to compare against and justify the choice.

content.markdown:
- **[Baseline 1]** — [why it is a fair comparison]
- **[Baseline 2]** — [state-of-the-art method]

children.title: Evaluation Metrics
children.objective: Define how success is measured and why these metrics are appropriate.

content.markdown: _Metrics, number of runs/seeds, confidence intervals and statistical tests used._

children.title: Reproducibility
children.objective: Give everything needed to reproduce the results.

content.markdown:
- **Hardware:** [GPU/CPU, memory]
- **Software:** [framework and versions]
- **Hyper-parameters:** [values and how they were selected]
- **Code and data:** [repository URL, DOI]

sections.title: Results
sections.objective: Report the findings objectively, organised by research question.

children.title: Main Results
children.objective: Answer the main research questions with the key tables and figures.

content.markdown:
| Method | Metric 1 ↑ | Metric 2 ↓ | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline 1 | … | … | … |
| **Ours** | **…** | **…** | … |

children.title: Ablation Study
children.objective: Show the contribution of each component of the approach.

content.markdown:
| Variant | Metric 1 | Δ vs full |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full model | … | — |
| w/o [component] | … | … |

children.title: Further Analysis
children.objective: Explore sensitivity, qualitative examples and failure cases.

content.markdown: _Sensitivity to hyper-parameters, qualitative examples, error analysis._

sections.title: Discussion
sections.objective: Interpret the results, their implications and their limits.

children.title: Interpretation and Implications
children.objective: Explain what the results mean for the research questions and the field.

content.markdown: _For each RQ: answer, evidence, and what it implies._

children.title: Limitations and Threats to Validity
children.objective: Discuss internal, external and construct validity honestly.

content.markdown:
- **Internal:** [...]
- **External:** [...]
- **Construct:** [...]

sections.title: Conclusion and Future Work
sections.objective: Close with the take-away message and the next steps.

content.markdown: _Restate the problem, the contribution and the main results in one paragraph; then two or three concrete future directions._

sections.title: Data and Code Availability
sections.objective: State where data, code and other artifacts can be found.

content.markdown:
- Code: [URL]
- Data: [URL / DOI]
- License: [...]

_Keep the bibliography (.bib) and related papers in References._
